message.content:
This is a cable assembly of insulated conductors with a connector on one end only, so it falls under heading 8544. Since it is fitted with connectors, it is not an 8544.49 "other" insulated conductor without connectors. The relevant subheadings are:

- 8544.42: other electric conductors, for a voltage not exceeding 1,000 V, fitted with connectors.
- 8544.42.90 covers other conductors fitted with connectors. 8544.42.20 is for conductors of a kind used for telecommunications, and 8544.42.90 is the residual line.
- The signals are electrical and not for communication, so the telecommunications line does not apply.

The statistical suffix is the uncertain part. The 8544.42.90 line has a 5% rate (actually 2.6%) with the suffix 8544.42.9090. I recall 8544.42.9090 as "Other", which is where this belongs.

Under that reading, a CBP ruling for a similar item would likely use 8544.42.9090.

```json
{"hts_code": "8544.42.9090", "reason": "Insulated electric conductors (<1000V) fitted with a connector on one end, not of a telecommunications type, fall in the residual 'other' line of 8544.42 under GRI 1."}
```
